question: Sanjana borrows ₹16,000 at 24% per annum simple interest and Savithri borrows ₹18,200 at 20% per annum simple interest. In how many years will their amounts of debts be equal?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Yearly Interest (Sanjana) = 16000 × 24% = 3840

Yearly Interest (Savithri) = 18200 × 20% = 3640

Difference in yearly interest = 3840 − 3640 = 200

Gap in initial amount = 18200 − 16000 = 2200

Years to equalize amount = 2200 ÷ 200 = 11 years

**∴ The correct option is (B).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (Sanjana) P₁ = ₹16,000 | Rate R₁ = 24% p.a.

Principal (Savithri) P₂ = ₹18,200 | Rate R₂ = 20% p.a.

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100
